market_context: U.S. futures are mixed: Nasdaq-100 futures are up roughly 0.4%-0.5% and S&P 500 futures are modestly higher, while Dow futures are lower. Treasury yields have surged, with the 10-year yield around 5.3%, creating a headwind for rate-sensitive equities; today’s calendar includes initial jobless claims, construction spending, S&P Global manufacturing PMI, and ISM manufacturing data. Premarket leadership is concentrated in selected technology and industrial names, while volatility remains elevated but moderate with VIX near 17.

predictions.reasoning: S&P 500 futures were modestly positive, approximately 0.1%-0.2%, suggesting a slightly higher open. However, the 10-year yield near 5.3% and elevated volatility create meaningful downside risk, so the expected gain is limited to roughly 0.3%.

Nasdaq-100 futures were up approximately 0.4%-0.5%, indicating continued relative strength in large-cap technology despite rising yields. QQQ may retain a modest bid if manufacturing data does not materially increase expectations for further Fed tightening.

Dow futures were reported lower by roughly 0.2%-0.4%, underperforming Nasdaq futures as rising Treasury yields pressure economically sensitive and value-oriented large caps. A modest decline is more likely than a sharp selloff because VIX remains below 17.

The technology-led futures setup favors semiconductor and high-growth exposure, and Nasdaq futures were materially stronger than Dow futures. The forecast is only modestly bullish because a 5.3% 10-year yield can compress high-growth valuation multiples and increase intraday reversals.
